plates.title: The Spine: From Question to Discovery
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, vellum-toned parchment with faded gold leaf accents, ink-and-wash figures in a medieval hand, arranged in a single column of eleven framed vignettes running top to bottom in strict reading order, connected by a thin flowing ribbon-path (like a river on an old map) that forks into four parallel branches at the middle and rejoins into one at the bottom. At the top: SIGNALS INTO BEHAVIOR shows a robed figure at a cave mouth with beams of light entering and a path leading onward. Below: TWO MEASURING TOOLS, two scribes at desks, one comparing matching scrolls, one watching an hourglass as a message passes. Next: FLOW IS NOT ENOUGH, a lone messenger on a road past an unread crossroads of letters. Next: CUTTING THE WHOLE, a master cutter slicing a glowing loaf at a workbench, with FIGURE A rendered as a small illuminated diagram of overlapping ovals pinned above. Next: TWELVE RIVAL RULERS, a council of twelve robed scholars arguing with scales. Next: THE NEEDLED SLICE, a tissue slice on a grid of fine needles each pricking up light, with FIGURE C as a small laboratory dish-and-bench scene beside it. Here the ribbon forks into four scenes side by side: THE WEALTHY HILL (bright houses on a hill above a dim village), THE LOOPED ROPE (two messengers tied together passing letters), THE CANDLE'S PEAK (a candle brightest at mid-distance on a table), MANY COPIES, ONE GRASP (a reaching hand amid many identical messenger pouches). The four branches rejoin into: THE DROWNED TALLY, a mapmaker buried under a teetering stack of labelled tiles, with FIGURE D as a small scattered chart at his feet. Final vignette at the bottom: READING THE PATTERN, a gatekeeper studying the arrangement of several banners before opening a gate. Palette restricted to sepia ink, faded blue-grey wash, and small touches of tarnished gold leaf. No lettering anywhere except the eleven capitalized titles, each lettered plainly beneath its vignette in an antique serif hand. Generous bare parchment margins; scenes large enough to read clearly, using the full width of the page, not crowded into a narrow column.

plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page in the same sepia-and-gold-leaf hand as the overview, a single vertical column of seven framed vignettes connected by a thin gold ribbon running straight down the page in strict order. Top: THE SACKS DON'T BALANCE, a merchant at a two-pan scale, one large sack opposing several small sacks that will not level. Next: WEAVING THE THREADS, a robed figure gathering loose threads into one new cord. Next: WILLIAMS AND BEER'S LEDGER, two scholars presenting an open ledger to a seated court, the ledger page showing a simple diagram of overlapping shapes rendered as exact sums. Next: TWO WELLS, ONE BUCKET, two wells pouring into a single bucket, with FIGURE A drawn faithfully as a small inset diagram of overlapping ovals held in a scroll beside the wells. Next: ONE KEY, FOUR LOCKS, a locksmith holding one key on a ring of four latches, three of them already clicking open. Next: THE SCAFFOLD GROWS, a builder staring up at an unsupported sprawling wooden scaffold far larger than the simple bridge he built before. Bottom: THE CLIMBING LATTICE, a stonemason setting small carved stones one by one into a tall climbing lattice of stone steps, with FIGURE B rendered faithfully as the lattice structure itself, drawn in thin ink lines as an architectural scaffold of interconnected nodes. Palette: sepia ink, faded blue-grey wash, small gold-leaf highlights on the ledger and the keys. No lettering anywhere on the page except the seven capitalized titles lettered beneath each vignette in an antique serif hand. Wide bare parchment margins, scenes spaced generously using the full width of the page, not cramped into a narrow strip.

plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, same sepia-ink and faded-gold-leaf hand as the previous plates, a single column of seven framed vignettes down the page joined by a thin ribbon-path that briefly forks into three side-by-side scenes at the middle and rejoins. Top: THOUSANDS OF MEETING POINTS, a cartographer marking convergence points on a dish of needled threads, with FIGURE C drawn faithfully as the laboratory dish and recording apparatus. Next: THE BOUND CURRENT, a ferryman rowing in a boat whose speed is tied by a visible cord to the river current. Here the path forks into three scenes: THE HILL'S BRIGHT HOUSES (grand glowing houses on a hill above dimmer valley houses), THE DOUBLE-ROPED PAIR (two messengers bound by a double rope with a brighter shared lantern beside an unroped pair), THE MODEST DISTANCE (a candle brightest at a middle point on a table, dimmer near and far). The three rejoin into: THE EXAGGERATED SHADOW, a surveyor's compass casting a shadow far longer than the pole it measures, with FIGURE D rendered faithfully as a small inset chart beside the surveyor. Bottom: THE REACHING HAND'S MANY RIDERS, a trained monkey reaching for a cup while many identical scrolls are loaded onto many departing riders. Palette: sepia ink, faded blue-grey wash, small gold-leaf touches on the lanterns and compass. No lettering anywhere on the page except the seven capitalized titles lettered beneath each vignette in an antique serif hand. Wide bare parchment margins, each scene large and clear, using the full width of the page rather than a narrow crowded strip.
